slides.headline: TypeSafe published *nine ways* their own model fails
slides.subhead: The feed has run the speed multiple for a week. The most useful thing the vendor shipped is the list of what breaks, and publishing it at all is more honest than most manage.

slides.headline: Before you wire it into *anything*
items: It answers the question you wrote, not the one you meant
It is not a calculator, and counting error grows with list length
Dates are read as text, not as ordered quantities

slides.headline: A question and its negation *summed to*
slides.body: Same ticket, two yes or no questions. Asking for a refund scored 0.72. Asking for anything else scored 0.47. They should sum to 1.

slides.headline: Scored against *two models*, not against truth
slides.body: An independent critique found the published evals score Jev against the average prediction of GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1. That measures agreement. It does not measure being right.

slides.headline: A typed output guarantees the *interface*, not the answer
Read the failure page before the benchmark
slides.body: Then re-measure on your own labelled data before you believe any multiple. That holds for every model anyone sells you this quarter.
slides.source: docs.typesafe.ai model jaggedness page, plus an independent eval critique
